items.title: Private Browser OCR Trades Data Egress for a New Kind of Operations Burden
items.summary: A browser-native OCR pipeline can render PDFs, detect text, recognize words, and extract entities without uploading sensitive documents. That removes a major privacy boundary, but shifts model delivery, memory pressure, browser compatibility, performance telemetry, and correctness onto the client.
items.angle: Long-form — evaluate local inference as an architectural trade rather than a privacy slogan, with a threat model and an operational checklist for deciding whether it is genuinely safer.
points: Compare the trust boundaries and data flows of hosted OCR with in-browser inference.
Account for model and WebAssembly download size, caching, startup latency, memory use, and mobile constraints.
Explain residual data-leak paths such as analytics, crash reporting, browser extensions, third-party scripts, and remote model assets.
Cover integrity controls for models and runtime artifacts, including pinning, hashes, CSP, and supply-chain review.
Define quality and performance telemetry that does not capture document contents.
Discuss fallback behaviour when WebGPU, WebAssembly features, or memory capacity are unavailable.

items.title: Artificial Beaver Dams Are Reliability Engineering for Rivers
items.summary: Artificial beaver dams reportedly raised juvenile coho salmon survival from 8% to 60%, making this a striking left-field example of redesigning system dynamics rather than optimizing individual components. The restoration work offers useful parallels with buffering, graceful degradation, redundancy, and designing around disturbances.
items.angle: Short post — use ecological restoration as a disciplined systems-engineering analogy, while being careful not to turn one reported result into a universal prescription.
points: Explain how small structural interventions can change flow, habitat, temperature, and refuge availability.
Compare dams and floodplains with buffers that absorb bursts and reduce downstream volatility.
Draw the distinction between improving component survival and changing the surrounding system conditions.
Relate habitat diversity to redundancy and multiple viable operating states.
Note the limits of the analogy and the need to test interventions in their local ecological context.
